The proposed answer of 1/10 is correct, and the argument holds up.

**Structure.** A vertex of $T_2(P_n)$ is a pair $\{a,b\}$ with $a<b$. Moving one token along an edge of $P_n$ changes $a$ or $b$ by $\pm1$ while keeping $a<b$. So $T_2(P_n)$ is exactly the grid graph induced on the triangular region $R=\{(a,b):1\le a<b\le n\}$. This region has $\binom n2$ vertices.

**Lower bound.** Every closed neighborhood in the grid has at most 5 vertices. So $\gamma \ge \binom n2/5 \sim n^2/10$.

**Upper bound.** The set $S=\{(x,y):2x+y\equiv 0 \pmod 5\}$ is a perfect dominating set of $\mathbb Z^2$. Restrict it to $R$. Any vertex of $R$ whose unique dominator in $S$ lies outside $R$ is adjacent to a point outside $R$, so it lies on the boundary of $R$. The boundary has $O(n)$ vertices, and adding each of them to the set costs $O(n)$ extra dominators. Hence $\gamma \le \binom n2/5 + O(n)$.

**Limit.** Combining the bounds, $\gamma = n^2/10 + O(n)$, so $\gamma/n^2 \to 1/10$.

The small-case checks in the proposed solution are loose, but they do not affect the asymptotic result.
